name: Maaseja
title: Priest Who Took a Foreign Wife
summary: Maaseja (also spelled Maasai or Maaseja) was a priest who lived in the period following the return from the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned among the priests who had taken foreign wives and were required to send them away as part of Ezra's reforms to preserve Israel's religious purity. His name appears in several lists of priests and Levites after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned Among the Priests Who Returned
keyEvents.description: Maaseja is mentioned among the priests and Levites who settled in Jerusalem after returning from the Babylonian exile.

keyEvents.title: Foreign Wives Among the Priests
keyEvents.description: Maaseja was one of the priests from the line of Jeshua who had taken foreign wives, which was contrary to God's law.

keyEvents.title: The Promise to Send Away the Foreign Wives
keyEvents.description: As part of Ezra's reform, Maaseja and the other priests made a promise to send away their foreign wives and bring a guilt offering.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's Reading of the Law
keyEvents.description: Maaseja was among those who stood beside Ezra as he read the Law of Moses to the people at the Water Gate, an important event in Jerusalem's spiritual renewal.

keyEvents.title: Participation in the Wall Dedication
keyEvents.description: Maaseja participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah's leadership, a milestone in the city's rebuilding.
